newsitem.title: KENYA: U.N. envoy to see rebel chief in rebel-held Zaire.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy to see rebel chief in rebel-held Zaire.

text.p: Kenya's foreign minister said on Thursday U.N. special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun would fly on Friday to rebel-held eastern Zaire to meet rebel leader Laurent Kabila.

Foreign Minister Kalonzo Musyoka said Sahnoun would try to secure Kabila's compliance to a call by African leaders in Nairobi on Wednesday for a Zaire ceasefire to pave the way for a negotiated settlement.
Kabila has rejected a ceasefire before negotiations with ailing Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, or a representative appointed by him, on how the Zairean leader will step down.

Asked what was the point as Zaire wanted a ceasefire before talks, Musyoka said: "I believe Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo would wish to have further consultations with President Mobutu on that subject."
Sahnoun is the special envoy of the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity to the Great Lakes region. Kengo, like Sahnoun, attended the one-day meeting on Zaire in Nairobi on Wednesday.
At a briefing, Musyoka also said he expected a Zairean government representative to attend a meeting, dubbed Nairobi Three, in Lome, Togo, on March 25, the eve of an OAU summit on Zaire.

Asked whether the Zairean government had therefore dropped its demand for a withdrawal of foreign forces from Zaire and international monitors to check on the pullout before attending the Nairobi Three summit, Musyoka indicated it might have.
Zaire has accused Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi of sending their troops into eastern Zaire to fight alongside the Tutsi -dominated rebels. All three countries have denied involvement.
